Empirical Research Plan:  Massachusetts Health Reform, 2006-2008

--------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------
Preferred design:  Difference-in-Differences (DiD) combined with an instrumental-variables second stage (2SLS-DiD).

• First stage (intensive margin):  Use the 2006 reform as an exogenous shock to insurance status.  The instrument is  Postt × HighPredUninsuredi, where  
  – Postt = 1 for claims filed after 1 July 2007 (date by which the coverage mandate was fully enforced), 0 otherwise;  
  – HighPredUninsuredi = 1 for individuals whose pre-reform predicted probability of being uninsured is above the median (constructed from 2006 data using age, zip-code poverty rate, race, and employment industry).

• Second stage (outcome):  Estimate the causal effect of (instrumented) insurance coverage on (i) hospital admissions and (ii) preventive-care visits.

Why appropriate?  
a.  The reform created a sharp discontinuity in the incentive to obtain insurance, plausibly unrelated to latent trends in individual health demand.  
b.  The high-vs-low predicted-uninsured split gives us a within-state control group, avoiding the need for out-of-state data.  
c.  The 2SLS step corrects for remaining selection in who actually takes up insurance.

--------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
INSUREDit = 1 if individual i is observed with any non-Medicare, non-Medicaid private or public insurance in year-half t, 0 otherwise.

Treatment timing  
Post reform = all claims with service dates on/after 1 July 2007.

Groups  
Treated (high-exposure): individuals in the top 50 % of pre-reform predicted uninsured probability.  
Control (low-exposure): individuals in the bottom 50 %.

Counterfactual  
Outcomes of the control group in the post-period proxy for treated outcomes had the reform not occurred.

--------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel-trends:  Absent the reform, hospital and preventive-care utilization for high- and low-exposure groups would have evolved similarly.  
  Plausibility: Both groups reside in the same state; we will provide evidence using 2006 pre-trend graphs and placebo tests (e.g., 2005 H2 vs 2006 H1).

A2. Exclusion (IV):  Post × HighPredUninsured affects utilization only through insurance status, not through other channels.  
  Plausibility: The mandate targets coverage. Potential violation—simultaneous safety-net hospital funding changes; we include hospital-fixed effects and local time-varying controls.

A3. Stable Composition:  No differential in- or out-migration across groups within the very short 2-year window.  
  Plausibility: Residential mobility across Massachusetts zip codes is low over 18 months; we can re-check with enrollment files.

A4. Stable Unit Treatment Value (no spillovers):  Gaining insurance for the treated does not crowd out provider capacity for the control.  
  Plausibility: Massachusetts hospitals operate below national occupancy; we will test for spillovers by estimating group-specific wait-time changes.

--------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
--------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Differential macro shock (Great Recession) in 2008  
• Mitigation: Include monthly state unemployment rate interacted with high-exposure indicator; restrict main window to July 2006–June 2008.

T2. Coding or reporting changes in claims following reform  
• Mitigation:  Include provider-year fixed effects; replicate outcomes using alternative claims sets (e.g., ED flag vs inpatient DRG counts).

T3. Mean-reversion/health shock selection (sicker individuals may sign up first)  
• Mitigation: 2SLS framework already addresses endogenous take-up; additionally, control for individual fixed effects where panel exists and run event-study plots to show no pre-trend.

--------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------
```r
#############################################
# 0.  Packages
#############################################
library(data.table)    # fast I/O
library(fixest)        # high-dim FE and IV
library(lubridate)     # date handling
library(ggplot2)

#############################################
# 1.  Load data
#############################################
claims <- fread("MA_APCD_2006_2008.csv")   # one row per claim

#############################################
# 2. Construct variables
#############################################
# Convert service date to half-year
claims[, date := ymd(service_date)]
claims[, halfyear := paste(year(date),
                           ifelse(month(date) <= 6, "H1", "H2"), sep = "_")]

# Pre-reform dummy
claims[, post := as.integer(date >= ymd("2007-07-01"))]

# Individual-level insurance flag (exclude Medicare/Medicaid duals)
claims[, insured := as.integer(insurance_type %in%
                    c("EMPLOYER_PLAN","EXCHANGE_SUBSIDIZED","OTHER_PRIVATE"))]

# Predict pre-reform uninsured probability (logit on 2006H2 only)
pre <- claims[halfyear == "2006_H2"]
logit_fit <- glm(insured ~ age + female + zip_poverty +
                 race_black + race_hisp + employment_industry,
                 family = binomial(link="logit"), data = pre)
claims[, pred_unins := 1 - predict(logit_fit, newdata = claims, type = "response")]

# High vs low exposure
median_cut <- quantile(pre$pred_unins, 0.5)
claims[, high_exposure := as.integer(pred_unins >= median_cut)]

# Instrument
claims[, z := post * high_exposure]

# Outcomes aggregated to individual-half-year level
outcomes <- claims[, .(
      hosp_adm = sum(claim_type == "INPATIENT"),
      prev_vis = sum(service_category == "PREVENTIVE_CARE"),
      insured = max(insured),                # any coverage
      z        = max(z),
      post     = max(post),
      high     = max(high_exposure)
), by = .(person_id, halfyear)]

#############################################
# 3.  Main IV-DiD regression
#############################################
# FE: person and half-year
ivreg <- feols(hosp_adm ~ 1 | insured ~ z | person_id + halfyear,
               data = outcomes, cluster = ~person_id)
summary(ivreg)

# Second outcome
ivreg_prev <- feols(prev_vis ~ 1 | insured ~ z | person_id + halfyear,
                    data = outcomes, cluster = ~person_id)
summary(ivreg_prev)

#############################################
# 4.  Event-study robustness check
#############################################
# Relative time in months to reform
claims[, rel_month := interval(ymd("2007-07-01"), date) %/% months(1)]
event <- feols(hosp_adm ~ i(rel_month, high_exposure, ref = -1) | 
               person_id + halfyear, data = outcomes, cluster = ~person_id)
iplot(event)   # should show flat pre-period coefficients
```

--------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------------------
Based on prior literature (e.g., Oregon Lottery, ACA Medicaid expansions):

Hospital admissions:  We expect a modest *decrease* (−3 % to −8 %) among newly insured due to substitution of emergency/inpatient care with outpatient management and better preventive access.

Preventive-care visits:  Expect an *increase* of roughly +15 % to +25 % per year for treated individuals (roughly one additional preventive encounter every 5–6 individuals annually).

--------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (1 = good, 0 = doubtful)
--------------------------------------------------------------
Parallel-trends visually confirmed? ...................... 0.8  
Exclusion restriction credible? .......................... 0.7  
No endogenous sample selection? .......................... 0.8  
Correct standard-error clustering? ....................... 1.0  
Robustness/Placebo tests planned? ....................... 0.9  

Overall:  4.2 / 5

--------------------------------------------------------------
